VAEE as Dictionary Learning — Intermediate Report

Workshop-paper track · v4 · phase: synthetic feature-recovery validation (2D tiers) · 2026-06-17

We validate VAEE as a dictionary-learning method on controlled 2D synthetic data with known ground-truth atoms, so recovery is measured directly: Hungarian matching of learned prototype directions to true atoms, reported as matched fraction (atoms recovered above cos 0.9) and mean cosine similarity. Three tiers form an escalating ladder defined by the coefficient / support structure: single atoms (easy) → binary superposition (medium) → continuous-magnitude superposition (hard). We then repeat the ladder in high dimension (D=32, K=64 atoms = 2× overcomplete, E[k]≈3) — the regime where MSE becomes a fair recovery proxy — and sweep within-concept variation (additive noise σ=0.05/0.10/0.20) on the hardest high-dim tier.

Reading the metrics. #active concepts is the per-sample count of firing concepts — the sparsity axis (the headline Pareto is MSE vs #active concepts, not raw L0). For VAEE a concept is an E-dimensional subspace (prototype + per-sample variation), so its true capacity is #active × E; an SAE latent is a 1-D ray (direction × scalar). Matched #active is therefore not matched capacity — a point we keep explicit when comparing MSE.

Findings so far (2D)

Headline. Standard VAEE is the only model whose recovery improves as the task gets richer — it fails the trivial tier but nails the hardest. On hard (continuous magnitudes) it is the only model that recovers atoms and reconstructs them well; SAEs reconstruct (trivially, in 2D) on a non-atomic basis, and VQ-VAE / β-VAE break.

Standard VAEE improves with difficulty — but it's a coverage story, not a ceiling

  • Recovery climbs easy ≤0.5 → medium 0.80 → hard 1.00 (best operating point), the inverse of every other model.
  • The easy failure is not a hyperparameter artifact: across ~15 prior runs (β, γ, λ_ent, λ_ortho sweeps) standard VAEE never beat 0.375 on the k=1 tier. The 2D plots show the mechanism — a prototype-coverage failure: some atoms get two prototypes, others get none ([1,1,1,2,0] instead of [1,1,1,1,1]). Nothing in the objective penalizes this: the orthogonality term acts in embedding space and is geometrically capped (you can't have 5 mutually-orthogonal directions in 2D), so there is no repulsion to spread prototypes onto all atoms. Coverage is left to initialization, hence seed-dependent.
  • Caveat: with only 5–8 atoms, matched fraction is quantized in steps of 0.125–0.2 and single-seed runs land in different coverage minima, so individual numbers carry a ±0.2–0.4 noise band. Multi-seed runs are required before any of these are stated as stable — flagged as a hard requirement for the camera-ready.

The per-sample encoder is the differentiator on continuous data

  • On binary tiers VAEE and VAEE-SE tie on recovery. On hard they both recover (matched 1.0) but separate on reconstruction: VAEE MSE 0.010 vs VAEE-SE 0.046. VAEE-SE's fixed prototype reconstructs (mean magnitude)·atom — a magnitude floor — while VAEE's per-sample μ(x) encodes the actual magnitude (the apple is "red", and μ carries this shade).
  • μ at inference is the free posterior mean (not sampled), so each active concept spans an E-dim subspace around its prototype. Its freedom to fit per-sample residual is rate-limited by the KL (β), not by capacity: a β-sweep shows MSE rising ~30× and #active concepts falling as β grows, and at β=1 VAEE drives MSE to ≈0.002. So VAEE can fit residual via μ; β sets how much.

Why the SAEs' near-zero MSE is not a quality signal (in 2D)

  • TopK/L1 reach MSE 10⁻⁴–10⁻⁷ but matched only 0.4–0.6. In 2D, two continuous active units span the whole plane, so the decoder fits any point — including the noise — on a non-atomic basis. MSE is degenerate here; recovery is the only honest axis.
  • VAEE's higher MSE is regularization-limited (KL), not capacity-limited — it has the parameters to overfit but the variational prior makes fitting noise cost more than it saves. This is exactly why the high-dim tiers matter: with k≈3 active in 32-D, k units cannot span the space, no model can noise-fit, and MSE becomes a fair recovery proxy.

Baselines

  • VQ-VAE recovers only by degeneracy: a fair codebook (size = #atoms) fails (matched 0.40, high MSE); it reaches 1.0 only by spending extra codes to memorise the discrete sample modes — and on continuous (hard) data even that degrades.
  • SAEs plateau at matched 0.4–0.6 (recover ~2 atoms, reconstruct the rest via mixtures).
  • β-VAE suffers posterior collapse (1–3 alive latents) and the worst MSE.
  • Overcomplete VAEE (K>atoms) self-prunes back toward the true atom count via its gate-KL (e.g. K=20→~5 alive) — encouraging for the "overcomplete + prune rare latents" direction, though it does not by itself fix the easy-tier coverage problem.

Findings — high-dim tiers (D=32, K=64)

Honest headline (this inverts the 2D story). In the fair, non-degenerate regime, TopK-SAE is the robust recovery winner: matched 0.92–0.98 at exactly k active concepts, on every tier. VAEE's 2D recovery advantage does not carry over — overcomplete VAEE is capped by latent/concept death (alive 18–44 of 64), and even with dead-latent resampling (alive→60–62) it reaches only matched≈0.53–0.72, below TopK. We report this plainly rather than cherry-picking the axis where VAEE leads.
  • TopK-SAE recovers cleanly and cheaply: matched ≈0.95 at #active = k (2–5), MSE degrading gracefully with k. It is the baseline to beat in high-dim and it is currently winning recovery.
  • L1-SAE is the degenerate noise-fitter: it posts the lowest MSE (10⁻³–10⁻⁴) but with a dense code (#active ≈ 27–33, half the dictionary) and poor recovery — though raising λ (0.3) trades MSE for recovery and reaches matched 0.84 on hard. Low MSE alone is not interpretability.
  • VAEE reaches matched 0.42–0.48 at the resample-off baseline, lifted to 0.53–0.72 by resampling (see next section). Its MSE (≈0.012) is competitive with TopK at the same operating point, but at more active concepts and lower recovery — so it does not dominate TopK on any single axis here.
  • VAEE-SE fails in high-dim continuous superposition (matched 0, cos≈0.29 ≈ the 32-D random-pair floor): a fixed prototype cannot absorb continuous per-sample magnitudes, so it spreads activation across many concepts and never locks onto atoms.
  • VQ-VAE and β-VAE both break in high-dim (matched ≈0; β-VAE collapses to 0–1 alive latents).
Single-seed caveat (unchanged, and load-bearing here). Every high-dim number is one seed; the recovery band is ±0.2–0.4. The qualitative ranking (TopK ≫ VAEE > VAEE-SE/VQ/β on recovery) is stable across configs, but the specific VAEE matched fractions are not camera-ready until the ≥3-seed reruns land.

Within-concept variation — does VAEE's per-concept lead widen with noise?

High-dim hard tier re-run at three additive-noise levels (σ = 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.20) with dead-latent resampling on. Additive noise is our (weak) proxy for intra-concept variation: samples sharing a concept support are no longer identical. The question was whether VAEE's reconstruction-per-active-concept advantage widens as within-concept variation grows.

Answer: no — the hypothesis is not supported. As σ grows, VAEE's recovery collapses (matched 0.67 → 0.38 → 0.00) and its #active concepts inflate (7 → 14), drifting toward L1's dense failure mode. TopK-SAE stays robust (matched 0.91–0.98 at k active throughout). VAEE is competitive only in the low-noise window; it does not pull ahead under within-concept variation, it falls behind.
  • L1-SAE's MSE decreases as noise rises (0.0005 → 0.0001) — the tell-tale signature of noise-fitting with a dense code; recovery stays 0.08–0.84 (λ-dependent). Not a real competitor on recovery.
  • The Pareto figure makes the multi-axis picture explicit: TopK owns the upper-left corner (few active concepts + high recovery) at every noise level. The "fewer concepts to inspect for a given reconstruction" claim does not hold here — at σ≥0.10 VAEE uses more active concepts than TopK, not fewer.
  • Why additive noise is the wrong test. Isotropic example-level noise is structureless: there is no shared low-rank direction for VAEE's per-sample μ to exploit, so μ can only fit it by burning rate (KL) or by recruiting extra concepts — exactly the degradation observed. The principled test is structured intra-concept variance (per-concept low-rank subspaces, x = Σ gateᵢ·(aᵢ + Bᵢwᵢ)), deferred to a make_complex_synthetic generator. The current result should be read as "additive noise hurts VAEE", not "VAEE has no within-concept-variation advantage" — the latter is untested.

Embedding size E is a capacity lever — and it rescues VAEE-SE

High-dim hard tier (σ=0.05), π fixed at 0.047, resampling on. Single seed — directional, not camera-ready. Capacity = #active × E.

The E=4 high-dim collapse was a gating-capacity artifact, not architectural. With K=64 prototypes crammed into a 4-D embedding space the gates cannot separate, so concepts never lock onto atoms. Enlarging E relieves this for both variants — and VAEE-SE goes from matched 0.00 (E=4) to 0.94 (E=64), becoming the best recoverer of the family.

  • Both saturate around E≈64 (VAEE 0.83→0.88, VAEE-SE 0.94→0.92, the dip within single-seed noise). TopK reference: matched 0.98, MSE 0.0127.
  • Clean variant split. VAEE-SE (fixed prototype, no per-sample μ) is the better recoverer (0.92–0.94, near TopK's 0.98) — it cannot fit per-sample magnitude, so it stays glued to atom directions; VAEE (per-sample μ) is the better reconstructor (MSE 0.0071, beating TopK) but blurs atoms via μ.
  • The honest cost: this near-parity costs ≈90× the capacity (E=128 ⇒ ~460 vs TopK's 5), on a dataset that is the linear-sparse SAE generative model. So it is expensive parity, not a win — the "loses badly to TopK" impression is an E=4 artifact, but the converse (a real VAEE win) this tier cannot produce.

Intervention (PLAN.md metrics 6 & 7) — and why this tier can't settle it

Ablation-based, model-agnostic (eval/intervention.py): for each active concept, zero its activation, decode, and measure the induced Δ. Consistency = mean resultant length of the unit Δ-directions across inputs (metric 6); causal matched / dominance = Hungarian match of mean Δ-directions to atoms + top/second-atom ratio (metric 7).

Intervention metrics, high-dim hard σ=0.05 (best E per VAEE variant; SAE at E=4)
modelconsistency ↑causal matched ↑dominance ↑
TopK-SAE (k=5)1.000.982.36
VAEE (E=128)0.990.892.22
VAEE-SE (E=64)1.000.922.12
L1-SAE (λ=0.3)1.000.841.59
The intervention metrics are correctly implemented but cannot reveal a VAEE advantage on this data — by construction. Two structural reasons:
  • Consistency is degenerate on a linear decoder. Ablating an SAE / VAEE-SE concept removes its fixed decoder column, input-independent ⇒ consistency = 1.000 trivially. VAEE is the only model below 1.0 (0.98), because its per-sample μ makes the direction wander — so the variational machinery slightly hurts the metric the plan expected it to win. Consistency only becomes informative with a nonlinear decoder (the plan's ResNet-feature-space metric 6), invisible here.
  • The metric reduces each concept to a single direction — the SAE-native object. It rewards 1-D concepts and is blind to VAEE's E-dim subspace. Causal-matched simply tracks prototype recovery for every model (the metric is self-consistent, not buggy), so the gap to TopK is just the recovery gap, which is the dataset.
VAEE's only edge here is dominance (interventions concentrate on one atom), and even that trails TopK. Verdict: on the linear-sparse tier, intervention favors the model whose inductive bias matches the generator (SAE). The variational-controllability claim must be tested where it can show — structured subspaces or nonlinear features.

In progress / pending

  • Structured intra-concept variance: make_complex_synthetic with per-concept low-rank subspaces (mixture-of-factor-analyzers, x = Σ gateᵢ·(aᵢ + Bᵢwᵢ)). Now the priority and the blocker: every result above is on the linear-sparse tier that is the SAE generative model, so it cannot produce a VAEE win. Only structured subspaces give VAEE's E-dim concept something a 1-D SAE latent cannot represent — the regime where recovery, MSE and intervention can all favor VAEE. A 2D-visualisable version is planned.
  • Multi-seed (≥3, ideally 5) on the key cells for mean ± std — the hard gate before any matched-fraction goes camera-ready. Decision taken: fix π = E[k]/K and sweep seed instead of π. Every E-sweep / noise / intervention number above is single-seed.
  • Nonlinear intervention: metric 6 in ResNet / LLM feature space, where the consistency metric is no longer degenerate and the variational posterior can pay off.
  • Coverage fix for standard VAEE on trivial 2D data (data-driven prototype init and/or an input-space repulsion term) — diagnosed, not yet implemented.
  • Image tiers (MNIST / Fashion-MNIST / dSprites) and the cross-dataset Pareto figure.
